newsitem.title: FRANCE: Christian Dior denies rupture with actress Beart.
newsitem.headline: Christian Dior denies rupture with actress Beart.

text.p: The Christian Dior fashion house denied reports on Thursday that it would not renew actress Emmanuelle Beart's contract because her support for illegal immigrants marred her image with Dior's well-heeled customers.

"Christian Dior denies this report. There's no rupture and her contract is not up for renewal," said a spokeswoman for LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, part of the business empire of luxury king Bernard Arnault.
The French organisation Movement Against Racism (MRAP) called on Thursday for a boycott of Christian Dior products.

"Dior...has refused to renew its exclusive contract with actress Emmanuelle Beart, saying her support for the Sans-Papiers (those lacking residence papers) at the Saint Bernard church was incompatible with her image as its representative," it said in a statement.

Beart, who starred in the French film "Manon of the Spring" and the Hollywood blockbuster "Mission Impossible", has joined in protests against deportation of illegal immigrants and other government actions to restrict immigration.
The cause of the Sans-Papiers, who include immigrants who arrived legally in France but have since lost the right to stay, has drawn strong support from artists, writers and actors.
Beart, considered one of France's most beautiful actresses, was hired to be the face of Dior in 1995.
Christian Dior perfumes and beauty products and the haute couture fashion house are controlled by Bernard Arnault's companies.
